- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., post-0.37 sentiment spikes).
- Underestimate when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.40 to -0.70) — model tends to ignore downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment turning.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast peaks if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Overshoot after positive sentiment spikes: if sentiment > 0.37 and price rises, cap forecast at 1–2% above peak to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is negative — reduce initial forecast by 0.5–1.5% for negative sentiment windows.
